Sure, here are two hints for the given step:

Hint 1: When one-hot encoding categorical variables, each unique category becomes a separate column in the design matrix. For the 'sex' column, which has two categories ('male' and 'female'), this will result in two columns. For the $$'embark_{town'}$$ column, which has five categories ('Southampton', 'Cherbourg', 'Queenstown', 'London', 'Oxford'), this will result in five columns.

Hint 2: Since we are not including an intercept term in the model, the design matrix will only consist of the one-hot encoded columns for 'sex' and $$'embark_{town'}$$. Therefore, the total number of columns in the design matrix $\Phi_3$ will be the sum of the columns from one-hot encoding 'sex' and $$'embark_{town'}$$.
